Triage: lands in `domain:spec` (`content/docs/protocol/kernel/**`); rationale: class (a) under the boundary in the rule — 「示例照抄即失败是 (a)」. These are JSON fences a client is meant to copy, and copying them fails: a client written from `error-handling.mdx` reads `data.error.details.retry_after`, gets `undefined` on **every** real 429, and falls back to its own default backoff. `Bug`.

⭐ **Which spelling is right was measured, not argued** — that is what makes this gradeable: `packages/runtime/src/endpoint-policy.ts` emits `details: { retryAfterSeconds, resetAt }`, and **two tests pin it** (`endpoint-policy.test.ts`, `dispatcher-plugin.endpoint-fallback.integration.test.ts`). ⇒ `http-protocol.mdx` matches the runtime; the other three sites do not. The disagreement is between two hand-written pages, and the producer breaks the tie.

`priority:p2` — 坏得安静, and the consequence is not confined to a confused reader. A client that silently ignores server-directed backoff on a rate-limit response **retries on its own schedule against a service that just asked it to wait**. That is the failure direction rate limiting exists to prevent, it is invisible at the client (no error, just a missing field), and it degrades exactly when load is already high. ⛔ Not p3 despite being "only docs".

⚠️ **The fence on this card is load-bearing and a mechanical fix will break it: ⛔ do not sweep `retry_after` globally.** The same token is a legitimate **`RetryStrategy` enum value** — `z.enum(['no_retry', 'retry_immediate', 'retry_backoff', 'retry_after'])` in `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts` — and `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx:47, 305, 391, 396` use it **correctly** in that sense. ⇒ Only the **`details` members** are wrong. A `sed` across the docs tree would corrupt four correct sites while fixing three wrong ones.

⚠️ **Verify before folding in the fourth site.** `realtime-protocol.mdx:1022` teaches `"retry_after": 5`, and the card is right to flag that realtime may have a **different emitter**. ⇒ Read that producer first: if it also emits `retryAfterSeconds`, it belongs in this fix; if it emits something else, it is a **second finding** and this PR should say so rather than quietly normalising it to match a producer it does not have.

⭐ Why nothing caught it, worth carrying into the PR so nobody assumes a gate will hold the fix: `details` is `z.unknown()` on the envelope, so **no schema constrains its members** and no gate compares a documented `details` key against what any producer emits; `os:check`'s type-check does not reach these either, because they are JSON fences rather than TypeScript. ⇒ After this lands the docs will be correct and still ungated — ⛔ do not describe the fix as "now enforced".

Scope: three sites in `error-handling.mdx` (`:418`, `:526`, `:650`) plus the reader instruction at `:734`, and the `realtime-protocol.mdx` site subject to the check above. `http-protocol.mdx:1126` is already correct — ⛔ do not touch it.

⛔ Correctly out of #15677's scope: that card is about the envelope key it renames, this is about the `details` bag, and the defect pre-exists on `origin/main`.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

⇒ ⛔ No `sed`, no global replace. Change only occurrences that are **members of a `details` bag**. Re-derive the four correct `error-catalog.mdx` sites yourself and show they are untouched in the final diff.

⚠️ **The fourth site is conditional and must be answered, not assumed.** Triage:

⇒ Read the realtime producer and state the reading. Either outcome is a good outcome; ⛔ guessing is not.

## Premises to re-measure, ⛔ none handed over as settled

Every line number in the card and in the triage comment was taken on an older `origin/main`. ⛔ Take yours from the tree, and give every zero-hit grep a positive control on the same file. Report the before/after occurrence counts per page, and the four `error-catalog.mdx` enum sites as an explicit **untouched** control.

⚠️ **Why this is p2 and not "only docs"** — carry it into the changeset, because it is the reason the card exists:

> A client that silently ignores server-directed backoff on a rate-limit response **retries on its own schedule against a service that just asked it to wait**.
